parts.title: A New Ice Age
parts.passageHtml:
{[A New Ice Age][211580]}

{[William Curry is a serious, sober climate scientist, not an art critic.][211585]} {[But he has spent a lot of time perusing Emanuel Gottlieb Leutze’s famous painting “George Washington Crossing the Delaware”, which depicts a boatload of colonial Ameriâ€‹can soldiers making their way to attack English and Hessian troops the day after Christmas in 1776.][211597]} {[“Most people think these other guys in the boat are rowing, but they are actually pushing the ice away,” says Curry, tapping his finger on a reproduction of the painting.][211639]} {[Sure enough, the lead oarsman is bashing the frozen river with his boot.][211659]} {[“I grew up in Philadelphia.][211673]} {[The place in this painting is 30 minutes away by car.][211679]} {[I can tell you, this kind of thing just doesn’t happen anymore.][211690]} {[”][211703]}

{[But it may again soon.][211706]} {[And ice-choked scenes, similar to those immortalised by the 16th century Flemish painter Pieter Brueghel the Elder, may also return to Europe.][211712]} {[His works, including the 1565 masterpiece “Hunters in the Snow”, make the now-temperate European landscapes look more like Lapland.][211735]} {[Such frigid settings were commonplace during a period dating roughly from 1300 to 1850 because much of North America and Europe was in the throes of a little ice age.][211756]} {[And now there is mounting evidence that the chill could return.][211784]} {[A growing number of scientists believe conditions are ripe for another prolonged cooldown, or small ice age.][211796]} {[While no one is predicting a brutal ice sheet like the one that covered the Northern Hemisphere with glaciers about 12,000 years ago, the next cooling trend could drop average temperatures 5 degrees Fahrenheit over much of the United States and 10 degrees in the Northeast, northern Europe, and northern Asia.][211812]}

{[“It could happen in 10 years,” says Terrence Joyce, who chairs the Woods Hole Physical Oceanography Department.][211864]} {[“Once it does, it can take hundreds of years to reverse.][211882]} {[” And he is alarmed that Americans have yet to take the threat seriously.][211894]}

{[A drop of 5 to 10 degrees entails much more than simply bumping up the thermostat and carrying on.][211909]} {[Both economically and ecologically, such quick, persistent chilling could have devastating consequences.][211928]} {[A 2002 report titled “Abrupt Climate Change: Inevitable Surprises”, produced by the National Academy of Sciences, pegged the cost from agricultural losses alone at $100 billion to $250 billion while also predicting that damage to ecologies could be vast and incalculable.][211941]} {[A grim sampler: disappearing forests, increased housing expenses, dwindling fresh water, lower crop yields, and accelerated species extinctions.][211985]}

{[The reason for such huge effects is simple.][212004]} {[A quick climate change wreaks far more disruption than a slow one.][212015]} {[People, animals, plants, and the economies that depend on them are like rivers; says the report: “For example, high water in a river will pose few problems until the water runs over the bank, after which levees can be breached and massive flooding can occur.][212026]} {[Many biological processes undergo shifts at particular thresholds of temperature and precipitation.][212071]} {[”][212084]}

{[Political changes since the last ice age could make survival far more difficult for the world’s poor.][212087]} {[During previous cooling periods, whole tribes simply picked up and moved south, but that option doesn’t work in the modern, tense world of closed borders.][212105]} {[“To the extent that abrupt climate change may cause rapid and extensive changes of fortune for those who live off the land, the inability to migrate may remove one of the major safety nets for distressed people,” says the report.][212131]}

{[But first things first.][212173]} {[Isn’t the earth actually warming?][212178]} {[Indeed it is, says Joyce.][212184]} {[‘In his cluttered office, full of soft light from the foggy Cape Cod morning, he explains how such warming could actually be the surprising culprit of the next mini-ice age.][212190]} {[The paradox is a result of the appearance over the past 30 years in the North Atlantic of huge rivers of fresh water – the equivalent of a 10-foot-thick layer – mixed into the salty sea.][212221]} {[No one is certain where the fresh torrents are coming from, but a prime suspect is melting Arctic ice, caused by a build-up of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere that traps solar energy.][212256]}

{[The freshwater trend is major news in ocean-science circles.][212289]} {[Bob Dickson, a British oceanographer who sounded an alarm at a February conference in Honolulu, has termed the drop in salinity and temperature in the Labrador Sea – a body of water between northeastern Canada and Greenland that adjoins the Atlantic – “arguably the largest full-depth changes observed in the modern instrumental oceanographic record”.][212299]}

{[The trend could cause a little ice age by subverting the northern penetration of Gulf Stream waters.][212342]} {[Normally, the Gulf Stream, laden with heat soaked up in the tropics, meanders up the east coasts of the United States and Canada.][212359]} {[As it flows northward, the stream surrenders heat to the air.][212383]} {[Because the prevailing North Atlantic winds blow eastward, a lot of the heat wafts to Europe.][212395]} {[That’s why many scientists believe winter temperatures on the Continent are as much as 36 degrees Fahrenheit warmer than those in North America at the same latitude.][212411]} {[Frigid Boston, for example, lies at almost precisely the same latitude as balmy Rome.][212439]} {[And some scientists say the heat also warms Americans and Canadians.][212454]} {[“It’s a real mistake to think of this solely as a European phenomenon,” says Joyce.][212466]}

{[Having given up its heat to the air, the now-cooler water becomes denser and sinks into the North Atlantic by a mile or more in a process oceanographers call thermohaline circulation.][212484]} {[This massive column of cascading cold is the main engine powering a deep-water current called the Great Ocean Conveyor that snakes through all the world’s oceans.][212514]} {[But as the North Atlantic fills with fresh water, it grows less dense, making the waters carried northward by the Gulf Stream less able to sink.][212540]} {[The new mass of relatively fresh water sits on top of the ocean like a big thermal blanket, threatening the thermohaline circulation.][212567]} {[That in turn could make the Gulf Stream slow or veer southward.][212589]} {[At some point, the whole system could simply shut down, and do so quickly.][212601]} {[“There is increasing evidence that we are getting closer to a transition point, from which we can jump to a new state.][212616]} {[”][212637]}

questionSets.title: Questions 1-4
questionSets.instructionHtml:
Choose the correct letter A, B, C or D.

Write your answers in boxes 1 - 4 on your answer sheet.

questions.text: The writer uses paintings in the first paragraph to illustrate

options.text: possible future climate change.
climate change of the last two centuries.
the river doesn’t freeze in winter anymore.
how George Washington led his troops across the river.

questions.explanationHtml:
B
​
Trong bài đọc, trong bức tranh vẽ, có cảnh các quân nhân ngồi trên 1 chiếc thuyền và đẩy các tảng băng ra xa mạn chuyền, do thời tiết năm 1776 qua lạnh nên nước biển đóng băng.
​
Cuối đoạn đầu tiên, có câu "I can tell you, this kind of thing just doesn’t happen anymore.” =>việc này không còn nữa
​
=> chọn B climate change of the last two centuries.

questions.text: Which of the following do scientists believe to be possible?

options.text: The temperature may drop over much of the Northern Hemisphere.
It will be colder than 12,000 years ago.
The entire Northern Hemisphere will be covered in ice.
Europe will look more like Lapland.

questions.explanationHtml:
Có thể thay 1 trong những đáp án bằng đáp án mới được tạo ra:
​
A fall in average temperature over the US, northern Europe, and northern Asia.

questions.text: Why is it difficult for the poor to survive the next ice age?

options.text: People don’t live in tribes anymore.
Politics are changing too fast today.
Abrupt climate change causes people to live off their land.
Migration has become impossible because of closed borders.

questions.explanationHtml:
D
​
Trong bài đọc, nói là, trong quá khứ, khi có sự thay đổi về thời tiết, các bộ lạc có thể tự do di chuyển qua vùng đất khác để ở. Tuy nhiên, trong thời đại ngày nay, các quốc gia đều có đường biên giới (closed borders), nên việc này sẽ gây khó cho người nghèo (the poor), những người sống dựa vào (live off) việc trồng trọt hoặc chăn nuôi.
​
=> D: Migration (di cư) has become impossible because of closed borders.

questions.text: Why is continental Europe much warmer than North America in winter?

options.text: Wind blows most of the heat of tropical currents to Europe.
Europe and North America are at different latitudes.
The Gulf Stream has stopped yielding heat to the air.
The Gulf Stream moves north along the east coast of North America.

questions.explanationHtml:
A
​
Trong bài đọc, có nói là "Gulf Stream" mang theo hơi nóng ở các vùng "tropics", và khi đi lên hướng Bắc, "Gulf Stream" sẽ "nhả" hơi nóng vào không khí "surrenders heat to the air". Vì gió North Atlantic thổi qua hướng Đông=> thổi hơi nóng qua Europe.

questionSets.title: Questions 5-9
questionSets.instructionHtml:
Look at the following statements (Questions 5-9) and the list of people in the box below. Match each statement with the correct person.

NB You may use any letter more than once.
questionSets.contentHtml:
Most Americans are not prepared for the next ice age. ______

The result of abrupt climate change is catastrophic. ______

The world is not as cold as it used to be. ______

Global warming is closely connected to the ice age. ______

Alerted people to the change of ocean water in a conference ______

options.text: William Curry
Terrence Joyce
Bob Dickson
National Academy of Sciences

questions.text: Most Americans are not prepared for the next ice age.
questions.explanationHtml:
B Terrence Joyce
Trong bài đọc nói là ông Terrence Joyce rất lo lắng (he is alarmed) khi người dân Mỹ chưa có quan tâm lắm đến mối nguy hiểm của biến đổi khí hậu.
Most Americans are not prepared for the next ice age. = rất nhiều người Mỹ chưa chuẩn bị sẵn sàng cho "thời kỳ băng giá" kế tiếp.

questions.text: The result of abrupt climate change is catastrophic.
questions.explanationHtml:
D

Trong bài đọc, có 1 báo cáo được viết bởi "National Academy of Sciences", nói là việc biến đổi khí hậu sẽ ảnh hưởng rộng và không thể đong đếm được => "catastrophic"

questions.text: The world is not as cold as it used to be.
Global warming is closely connected to the ice age.
questions.explanationHtml:
B

Trong bài đọc, Joyce nói là việc Trái Đất ấm lên có thể là 1 nguyên nhân bất ngờ (surprising culprit) của việc xuất hiện của thời băng giá mới.

=>Global warming is closely connected to the ice age. = Việc Trái Đất ấm dần lên liên hệ mật thiết (closely connected) với kỳ băng giá.

questions.text: Alerted people to the change of ocean water in a conference
questions.explanationHtml:
C

Trong bài đọc, Bob Dickson đã cảnh báo / "dấy lên hồi chuông" ( sounded an alarm) về việc giảm độ mặn và nhiệt độ của nước biển tại 1 hội nghị (conference​

Alerted (=sounded an alarm) people to the change of ocean water in a conference => cảnh báo mọi người về sự thay đổi của nước biển tại 1 hội nghị.

questionSets.title: Questions 10-13
questionSets.instructionHtml: Complete the flow chart below.  Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 10-13 on your answer sheet.

questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án câu 11: denser
​
Trong bài đọc, sau khi đã "nhả" hơi nóng ( Heat) vào không khí, nước sẽ đậm đặc hơn (denser) và chìm (sinks).

fresh water
​
Trong bài đọc, dòng chảy sâu này (deep-water current) chảy đến biển North Atlantic, và ở đây thì nhiều "fresh water" => làm cho dòng chảy bị loãng "less dense"
